title: Implement telemetry-driven surge-smoothing and guided customer communications for hosted-5xx waves
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Several high-severity customer escalations during recent production windows traced to multi-tenant hosted API 5xx waves. Root pattern: short bursts of connection/fanout pressure at the edge cause increased backend tail latency, which combined with client SDK retries and per-request fanout into multiple runtime shards leads to amplified request storms and transient KV cache churn. This ticket implements a telemetry-driven surge-smoothing layer plus a guided communications playbook so we can (a) blunt amplification quickly, (b) preserve SLOs for high-priority tenants, and (c) standardize customer messaging during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant surge score exposed in Console and Datadog within 60s of onset
Edge admission controller enforces a smoothing window that reduces immediate backend fanout by >=40% under test load
Default SDK retry policy doc updated and a temporary client advisory shipped to affected customers
Canary rollout of smoothing logic to 10% of traffic with no customer-visible increase in error rate
Reusable customer messaging templates live in Confluence and accessible from the incident runbook
steps_taken: Feb 12: Initial triage — correlated 5xx spikes with edge connection pool saturation and amplified retries; assembled cross-functional triage (SRE, runtime, SDK)
Feb 13: Short-term mitigation deployed: edge-side aggressive keepalive reclaim and a proxy-level slow-start admission gate (hotfix) — reduced immediate error rate by ~28% for observed tenants
Feb 14: Added detailed tagging on request context (tenant_id, route, sdk_version, retry_count) and shipped expanded telemetry to Datadog dashboards
Feb 17: Implemented a first-pass tenant leaky-bucket admission algorithm and performed load tests simulating mixed-tenancy surges
Feb 18: Created customer comm templates and incident checklist in Confluence; notified three affected customers with mitigation plan and ETA
next_steps: Finalize adaptive smoothing algorithm (moving-average + priority boost for SLA tiers) and loop in product for policy defaults
Roll out smoothing to 25% canary traffic and collect telemetry for 48 hours
Coordinate with SDK team to publish a recommended temporary retry configuration and an explanatory changelog entry
Implement automatic route-level fallback to Dedicated fastpath for customers with matching contracts and high surge score
Run tabletop with Solutions and Support to validate customer comm flow and SLAs
comments: 2025-02-12 Diego Morales: Found a correlation between edge connection queue growth and increased backend retries. Spike happened after a third-party client started a bulk job. Repro script saved in /playbooks/repro-edge-surge.md.
2025-02-13 Priya Shah (SRE): Hotfix reduced immediate 5xxs but deferred some load to long-tail latency — we need the smoothing window to preserve P95.
2025-02-15 Marcos Rivera (Runtime): KV cache churn observed in long sequences; adding pre-eviction cooldown to batch compaction helped in staging.
2025-02-18 Jenna Liu (Product): Will review policy defaults tomorrow. Need clear opt-in for Dedicated fastpath to avoid unexpected billing impacts for customers.
2025-02-19 Support Handoff: Templates reviewed; added a short FAQ and guidance on when customers should switch SDK retry toggles.
postmortem_notes: Primary cause: simultaneous client retries + proxy fanout under short-lived upstream congestion
Secondary cause: default SDK retry settings lacking built-in jitter and tenant-awareness
Operational gap: no easy way in Console to surface tenants approaching surge thresholds — added task to address UX
communication_plan: Notify affected customers with tailored advisory within 2 business hours of incident detection
Provide temporary recommended SDK settings and step-by-step rollback guidance
Offer Dedicated fastpath evaluation for customers with contractual needs; include cost/latency tradeoffs
Post-incident summary and action items to be posted to Customer Success and attached to customer ticket
